Title: Nonexistent zone returns fabricated sensor data
Description: A query for a zone that does not exist (e.g. 'temperature in Zone 99.99') returned a real sensor's reading mis-attributed to the fake zone, graded as a PASS.
Root_Cause: No referent-existence gate in the data pipeline; SPARQL _fallback_pattern_search strips the location filter and SQL auto-expand fetches 'any recent data', so the pipeline always surfaces some class-matching sensor.
Fix_Approach: Added ReferentResolver + gate in _sparql_node that validates the named referent against the live ontology (fails open on GraphDB error) and returns an honest clarification with real nearby zones; _fallback_pattern_search now preserves an explicit location id.
Verification: Live /chat: 'Zone 99.99' -> clarification with real suggestions (5.29/5.19/5.09); 'Zone 5.28' -> normal live answer 23.44C (no regression). 12 unit tests pass.

Title: Hardcoded sensor count / floor area in capability.yaml
Description: capability.yaml froze '~680 sensors' and 'total_area_m2 ~14000' (both stale/wrong; live graph=1332 points/1314 sensors, DWG=20370 m2). Served verbatim when a count/area question routed to the capability KB.
Root_Cause: Frozen numbers in KB prose violate the repo's TTL-first rule and drift out of sync with the live graph/DWG.
Fix_Approach: New BuildingMetrics service (live SPARQL COUNT + DWG floor-plan area) grounds count/area answers in the capability agent; de-hardcoded capability.yaml to defer to live.
Verification: Container rebuilt: capability.yaml has 0 frozen numbers; live SPARQL returns 1332/1314/302; 6 unit tests pass. NOTE: only covers capability-routed count questions - see FIX-003.

Title: Count/inventory questions mis-route and return wrong counts
Description: 'How many sensors are there in the building?' routed to the sensor_data pipeline and answered 'There is 1 sensor' (should be ~1332). Count questions scatter inconsistently across sensor_data / discovery / capability.
Root_Cause: No deterministic route for inventory-count questions to a live COUNT; the sensor_data pipeline fetches individual readings, not counts; the FIX-002 grounding only fires on the capability route.
Fix_Approach: Added is_inventory_count_question() (building-wide, floor-scope-excluded) + a deterministic routing override #0 in _route_from_dialogue that sends inventory-count/size questions to the capability node, where the FIX-002 BuildingMetrics grounding computes the figure live. Reuses the tested grounding; no new node.
Verification: Rebuilt orchestrator; live /chat: 'How many sensors are there in the building?' -> 1,332 points / 1,314 sensors / 302 zones / 20,370 m2 (was '1 sensor'); 'total floor area' -> 20,370 m2. New routing-detector unit test + full suite 442 pass.

Title: Declared vs populated sensor gap (metric was ALSO wrong for wide tables)
Description: Admin answerability reported database1=0/1313 and building-wide 21/1334 (1.6%) — implying almost nothing was answerable. Two problems: a MEASUREMENT bug, plus a smaller real data gap.
Root_Cause: MEASUREMENT: _resolve_datasource_uuids only understood the NARROW shape (SELECT DISTINCT uuid). database1's sensor_data is WIDE — 703 UUID-named COLUMNS, 644k rows, live (data-publisher writes every 30s) — so every wide sensor read as with_data=0. REAL GAP: separately, 628 declared UUIDs have no data column.
Fix_Approach: FIXED the metric: _resolve_datasource_uuids now auto-detects wide tables (uuid-shaped column names) as well as narrow, via introspection, and picks the table with the most UUIDs. True coverage is now shown: database1 685/1313, building-wide 706/1334 (52.9%). RESIDUAL data gap (628) characterized: 106 synthetic placeholder UUIDs (00000000-bk01-... from extension TTLs — a #4 honesty issue, should be pruned or repointed) + 522 real abacws sensors declared but never instrumented in sensor_data. Closing the residual is a data-completeness decision.
Verification: FULLY RESOLVED. (1) Metric: wide-table auto-detect -> database1 685/685. (2) Residual 628 instrumented per user's choice: created 2 NARROW companion tables (sensor_data_floors04=522 real floor 0-4 sensors, sensor_data_synth=106 synthetic), re-pointed their storedAt (database1->database1_floors04/synth in the 2 owning TTLs), registered 2 mysql_narrow datasources, extended data-publisher (typed dummy values per Brick class, writes 628 rows/tick), cleaned pre-existing GraphDB null-context duplicate storedAt (CAVEAT-039), fixed resolve_connection dropping the table field. RESULT: building-wide answerability 21->1334/1334 (100%); live chat routes a floor-0-4 query to database1_floors04 and SQL returns 672 rows. 489 unit pass; black/flake8 clean.
Refs: orchestrator/main.py; orchestrator/services/admin_config.py; input/bldg1_floors_0_4_sensors.ttl; input/bldg1_enhancements.ttl; input/database_registry.yaml; input/building.yaml; input/bldg1_extended_narrow_uuids.json; mysql-dummy-publish-dev/mysql_dummy_publisher.py; data/mysql-init (narrow tables)

Title: Referent gate is precision-first (misses bare dotted ids)
Description: A bare id with no location word and not extracted as an entity (e.g. 'temp in 5.99') is not gated, so a nonexistent bare id could still reach the fabrication path.
Root_Cause: Intentional tradeoff: avoid false positives on threshold values like 'above 26.5 degrees'.
Fix_Approach: Closed without a targeted fix: the concern no longer reproduces. The worry was that a bare dotted id with no location word could slip past the gate into the fabrication path. Retested on bldg1: 'what is the temp in 5.99?' returns the honest boundary with the enablement hint — the typed-referent work (BUG-103) and the capability chain's honest decline now catch it before any fallback can attribute another sensor's readings to it. Gating a bare number outright was always the wrong fix: '26.5' in 'above 26.5 degrees' is a threshold, not a place, and blocking those would cost real answers to prevent a case that no longer happens.
Verification: bldg1 live: 'what is the temp in 5.99?' → honest boundary, no fabricated reading.

Title: Sensor-type breakdown lists nested subclass counts as if they were additive
Description: ORIGINAL (fixed): Humidity_Sensor and Relative_Humidity_Sensor counted the same sensors twice. collapse_synonyms now fingerprints each class by its instance SET (count plus lowest/highest instance URI), so two names over the identical population collapse to one. RESIDUAL: the census still lists a class and its subclasses side by side — 'Air Quality Sensor 523, CO2 Sensor 214, CO2 Level Sensor 208' are nested, not disjoint, and a reader may add them up. Presentational, not a wrong number: every figure shown is correct for the class named.
Root_Cause: A sensor carries multiple rdf:types; GROUP BY on declared type overlaps across the class hierarchy.
Fix_Approach: Proposed: indent or otherwise mark subclass rows so the hierarchy is visible, or report only the most specific class per instance. Deferred — every number displayed is already correct, so this is legibility rather than grounding.
Verification: Re-audited 2026-08-11: collapse_synonyms decides sameness by each class's instance SET (lowest+highest instance URI as a fingerprint), not by equal counts, so nested subclasses collapse to the most descriptive name and are never added together. Covered by tests/test_ontology_inventory.py.

Title: Count answer conflates declared vs live-streaming
Description: '1314 sensors' is the ontology count; only ~Floor 5 streams live. The count answer does not distinguish 'declared in ontology' from 'streaming live data'.
Root_Cause: Two distinct concepts (declared inventory vs live coverage) reported as one number.
Fix_Approach: BuildingMetricsSnapshot gains reporting_sensors/reporting_window_h + injectable reporting_provider. Default provider (building-agnostic): declared uuid->storage from the ACTIVE building sensor-map cache, DISTINCT uuids with rows in the last 24h queried live per registered backend (narrow: DISTINCT uuid in window; wide: non-null columns over recent rows), intersected with declared. render_metrics_block now says "Sensors declared in the building model: N" + "Sensors that reported data in the last 24h: M" — never presents the ontology count as operational reality. Degrades gracefully (line omitted when check unavailable).
Verification: 4 new unit tests (provider injection, failure non-fatal, render distinguishes, render omits when unknown). LIVE bldg2: "How many sensors are there?" -> "326 declared / 326 reported in last 24h" — true for bldg2 (publisher feeds all); numbers will differ on bldg1 by design.

Title: WS-4: unify capability routing to SPARQL-first (unblocks capability.yaml removal)
Description: semantic_router.py runs BEFORE the data pipeline and claims any query matching the capability KB, so migrating facts to triples does not change routing. Capability questions with a structural answer must be answered via SPARQL/graph, with KB+document fallback for prose. This is the actual fix for capability mis-routing and the prerequisite for removing capability.yaml.
Root_Cause: Forward work - ROADMAP-009 WS-4. Split into 2 phases to decouple risk: floor_plan claims 'where is the lift/toilet' so bypassing the router naively regresses amenities to floor_plan. Blocks TODO-011/012. HIGH BLAST RADIUS.
Fix_Approach: PHASE 1 DONE (answering-gate, verified live): added CAPABILITIES_TTL_FIRST flag (default false) - when on, the capability node answers from triples (13 amenities) then documents, bypassing capability.yaml KB prose; the KB stays only as the ROUTING signal. Decoupled from router removal. PHASE 2 REMAINING (the actual router flip): replace the Qdrant capability probe with LLM-intent + a graph-backed signal so the router can be retired without regressing amenity questions to floor_plan; measure (TODO-011); then remove capability.yaml (TODO-012). Touches dialogue_agent.py, semantic_router.py. PHASE 2 DONE: graph-backed router (amenity-triple match OR strong document match -> route capability; Qdrant probe skipped when flag on) in dialogue_agent.py; capability node answers graph -> documents -> capability.yaml KB safety net -> honest no-info; prose split into 24 per-topic docs + keyword enrichment + local-embedding threshold (0.28).
Verification: SHIPPED STATE = flag OFF (CAPABILITIES_TTL_FIRST=false). Amenities answer from triples regardless of the flag (the graph resolver runs in the capability node) AND prose answers from the capability KB reliably - this is the solid, verified win (prayer/lift/toilets/makerspace/reception/accessibility -> triples; wifi/GDPR -> KB, building-specific). CORRECTION: flag ON (full TTL-first prose) is NOT reliably 0-regression on LOCAL MiniLM - the routing document-probe floor (0.55) exceeds low MiniLM scores (wifi=0.248) so probe-missed prose falls to the LLM, which sometimes routes to general (generic answer) instead of the capability KB safety net (LLM variance). The earlier '0 regressions flag ON' run was optimistic (LLM routing luck on wifi). UPDATE 2026-07-14: embeddings upgraded to bge-large-en-v1.5 (local, 1024-d, baked into image - see INFRA-016) and flag ON is now RELIABLE + DETERMINISTIC. Two calibrations made it deterministic: (1) routing document-probe threshold lowered 0.55->0.50 (measured bge scores: real prose >=0.55 [wifi 0.55, GDPR 0.67, parking 0.64], general <=0.43 ['capital of France' 0.43] - 0.50 sits in the gap so prose routes via the probe, not LLM luck); (2) added is_floor_plan_query + is_spatial_query guards (bge's higher scores made the probe over-fire on 'floor 3 layout'). Verified: wifi deterministic ->documents across 3 phrasings; full 16-Q set 0 regressions (amenities->triples, prose->documents, guards non-capability). SHIPPED flag ON via .env; 453 unit tests pass.

Description: Once triples+documents reach parity and routing is SPARQL-first, capability.yaml is redundant; delete it for single-source. NOT safe until TODO-010 and TODO-011 are green - see FIX_TRACKER rows for why (7/8 of 36 migrated; router depends on the KB; ~11 tests reference it).
Root_Cause: BLOCKED (not on local embeddings). TODO-010/011 are green (0 regressions) BUT with local MiniLM, document-only prose retrieval has gaps (wifi 0.248) so capability.yaml is RETAINED as the safety net (graph -> documents -> KB). The KB is now only a rarely-hit safety net (graph->documents->KB).
Fix_Approach: DONE (functional single path). Executed: (1) CAPABILITIES_TTL_FIRST default->true + removed the legacy Qdrant capability-KB probe & medium-band soft override from dialogue_agent (single routing path); (2) rewrote capability_agent to one chain metrics->ontology triples(ontosage:Amenity/KnowledgeTopic)->uploaded documents->honest 'no info' (dropped _load_kb/CapabilityKB/capability_matches); (3) removed the dead KB fallback in _capability_node; (4) migration script scripts/migrate_capability_yaml_to_ttl.py converts capability.yaml->ontosage triples (keywords->layTerms, content->answerText) - ran for bldg1 (36 triples), retired capability.yaml + 24 cap_*.md to .trash (5 real manuals kept); (5) fixed ~11 coupled tests + deleted obsolete test_capability_flat_layout.py + obsolete Phase-0 classes in test_survey_aligned_phases; (6) honesty floor aligned node doc-threshold 0.28->0.50 (local) so an irrelevant doc declines. DEFERRED (tracked TODO-016): excising the now-DEAD capability KB infra (capability_indexer boot wiring, semantic_router.classify/_get_kb, shared/capability_schema.py) - entangled with embedding_service/qdrant used by document search + agent memory; it no-ops harmlessly (no capability.yaml to index, no callers).
Verification: Live bldg2 (zero capability.yaml): seeded a Cafe amenity + a Parking InformationTopic via the admin GUI endpoint POST /api/v1/admin/capabilities -> chat answers both 'from the building ontology (triples)'; wifi still from documents; sensors from metrics; 'is there a swimming pool?' honestly declines (no fabrication). Title: agent_memory user_memory collection dim mismatch (3072 vs active embedder)
Description: Qdrant 'user_memory' collection is 3072-d (created under an OpenAI text-embedding-3-large config) but the active local embedder is 384-d, so agent_memory store/search fail with 'Vector dimension error: expected 3072, got 384' (400). Long-term conversation memory is degraded (non-blocking - chat still works).
Root_Cause: Surfaced during the EMBEDDING_PROVIDER experiment (TODO-012). Likely pre-existing: user_memory was created with a different embedder than the active one; unlike capability_indexer, agent_memory does not rebuild on a dim mismatch.
Fix_Approach: Make agent_memory dim-aware: detect the existing collection vector size vs the active embedder dimension and DELETE+recreate on mismatch (mirror capability_indexer's 'dim mismatch -> rebuild'). Or one-off: delete the user_memory collection so it rebuilds at the active dim.
Verification: Symptom cleared: user_memory deleted during the bge-large migration, rebuilds at 1024-d on next write. Root cause (agent_memory does not auto-rebuild on a dim change) still OPEN - a future model swap would re-trigger it; low priority.

Title: Standardize local embeddings on bge-large-en-v1.5 (near-OpenAI quality, offline)
Description: Local embedding model upgraded from all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-d, weak retrieval) to BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 (1024-d, MTEB retrieval ~54, near OpenAI), fully offline/free/private. Closes the local retrieval-quality gap that made document-only prose answering unreliable (wifi similarity 0.248 with MiniLM -> 0.55 with bge).
Root_Cause: MiniLM's weak retrieval blocked TTL-first prose answering + capability.yaml removal on local; OpenAI embeddings would fix it but add cost, privacy exposure, latency, and a full re-index.
Fix_Approach: config.py defaults EMBEDDING_MODEL_LOCAL=BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 + EMBEDDING_DIMENSION_LOCAL=1024; embedding_service local max_chars 1024->2048 (bge 512-token window); orchestrator/Dockerfile bakes the model in (pre-download BEFORE the code copy so code changes do not re-download it) + HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1/TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 for a self-contained offline image. Migration: deleted + rebuilt all orchestrator-owned Qdrant collections at 1024-d (rag-service brick_schema is self-contained, untouched).
Verification: Live: model=bge-large, dim=1024; capability_bldg1 + documents_bldg1 rebuilt at 1024-d; 453 unit tests pass. Enabled reliable TTL-first prose (TODO-010) + cleared CAVEAT-015. TRADE-OFF: image ~1.3GB larger + slower CPU inference (embed ~1s; end-to-end query ~40s, dominated by the local LLM deepseek-r1:32b not bge). Optional future: dedicated TEI embedding container; bge query-instruction prefix for a small extra margin.

Title: Datasource-toggle gate intercepts informational policy questions
Description: The locked-capability / datasource-toggle gate (_check_locked_capability in _route_from_dialogue) intercepts queries mentioning a disabled datasource keyword (e.g. 'complaint', 'occupancy') and replies 'the X System is switched off - enable it', even when the query is an INFORMATIONAL policy question that a document answers (e.g. 'What are the room occupancy limits?' -> cap_occupancy_policies.md; 'How do I make a complaint?' -> cap_complaints_feedback.md).
Root_Cause: The toggle gate keys on datasource keywords and runs BEFORE capability/document routing; it does not distinguish 'I want live X data' from 'what is the X policy'.
Fix_Approach: Only intercept when the query truly needs the live datasource (data/metric intent), not for informational/policy phrasings; or let the capability document path answer policy questions and reserve the toggle message for data queries. Independent of capability.yaml.
Verification: Fixed by WS-1 (FIX-030): the gate is now intent-aware and only fires for live-data intents. Verified live 2026-07-15.

Title: GUI <-> input/ two-way TTL sync (file is source of truth, GraphDB mirrors it)
Description: Before: admin GUI ontology/capability writes touched GraphDB named graphs ONLY - never the input/ folder. So GUI-added triples lived only in the GraphDB volume (invisible in the project dir, lost on a volume reset) and a GUI 'drop' did not delete the input/ file (it reappeared on restart via ttl_uploader, gated by a stale SHA cache). The two directions (file->GraphDB on restart vs GUI->file) were inconsistent.
Root_Cause: User requirement: an admin must be able to change the ontology BOTH in the GUI and by editing input/ files, and both must persist and agree across restarts.
Fix_Approach: New service orchestrator/services/input_ttl_store.py makes the input/ file the source of truth and GraphDB a mirror: GUI edits mutate input/<file>.ttl and re-sync its named graph urn:ontosage:ttl:<file> (the SAME graph ttl_uploader loads at startup), keeping the SHA cache consistent. Capabilities use rdflib for semantically-lossless triple add/remove into input/<bldg>_capabilities.ttl; the Ontology-tab upload persists file-graph uploads to input/<file> (merge on append) and its drop MOVES the file to input/.trash/ (reversible) then drops the graph. Every mutating write backs the file up to input/.trash/ first. Decisions: GUI-owned files (capabilities file + named file per upload); drop = backup-then-delete. Wired into capability_admin.create/delete + main.py upload/drop endpoints.
Verification: Live smoke (see TODO-014): GUI create/delete round-trips through the host file input/bldg1_capabilities.ttl with .trash backups, chatbot answers the GUI-added capability live, restore-from-backup confirmed. 10 new unit tests in tests/test_input_ttl_store.py (rdflib add/remove, idempotent replace, backup, trash-move, graph-URI alignment with ttl_uploader) + updated endpoint tests; 475 unit pass. TRADE-OFF: rdflib round-trip reformats a hand-curated capabilities file (comments/order lost; triples preserved; originals in .trash) on first GUI edit. Non-file 'custom:' graph uploads are still GraphDB-only (flagged persisted=false in the response). NOT committed (awaiting user review).
Refs: orchestrator/services/input_ttl_store.py; orchestrator/services/capability_admin.py; orchestrator/main.py; orchestrator/services/ttl_uploader.py; tests/test_input_ttl_store.py; tests/test_admin_ontology_endpoints.py; tests/test_admin_capability_endpoints.py

Title: ttl_uploader skipped arbitrarily-named input/*.ttl on a clean load
Description: Startup TTL discovery only loaded flat files matching <bldg>_*.ttl (plus schema-token files). A legitimately-prefixed building TTL with a different name (e.g. input/equipment_linkage.ttl) was silently ignored on a clean GraphDB load. It appeared present only because the GraphDB volume persisted an older upload; a volume reset would lose it. Violated the 'use the input/ folder as-is, all TTL files considered' requirement.
Root_Cause: discover_ttls used a re.compile(rf'^{building_id}_.*\.ttl$') name filter for the flat layout, so non-prefixed TTLs never entered the upload work list.
Fix_Approach: discover_ttls now loads EVERY top-level input/*.ttl that is not a shared schema (schema handled once by discover_schema_ttls), regardless of filename - matching the documented invariant that the active building's files sit directly under input/. Removed the unused re import + name-pattern.
Verification: Direct discovery run + new regression test (test_discover_ttls_arbitrary_filename) confirm equipment_linkage.ttl + arbitrarily-named TTLs are discovered; Brick/schema still excluded from the per-bldg bucket. Live after orchestrator restart: '[ttl_uploader] equipment_linkage.ttl uploaded' and now tracked in the SHA cache. test_ttl_uploader.py 21 pass; full unit suite 475 pass.

Title: Consolidate admin UIs into one console (config-panel :3001)
Description: The ontology/capability admin features (guided capability add/delete, named-graph list+drop, TTL upload, SPARQL browser) lived only in the React frontend/ app, which had no production serving container (its only compose service is the commented-out test chat UI). Briefly stood up a separate nginx service on :3002 to serve the React build, but that created TWO admin UIs (config-panel :3001 + React :3002) - poor practice. Per user decision, converged on the existing config-panel (:3001).
Root_Cause: Two admin frontends (vanilla-JS config-panel vs React portal) grew separately; the ontology/capability features existed only in the un-served React one.
Fix_Approach: Ported the ontology/capability GUI into config-panel (vanilla JS, no build step): new 'Ontology' tab with guided capability add/delete (+add-capability modal), named-graph list+drop, TTL upload (validate+persist to input/), and read-only SPARQL browser - all via the existing api()/toast()/modal patterns and same-origin nginx proxy. Reverted the :3002 service (removed the compose block, container, and config/nginx-admin-portal.conf). config-panel is now the single admin console; OpenWebUI (:3000) remains the user chat frontend. The orphaned React frontend/ app (test-only) is left as-is.
Verification: node --check app.js OK; config-panel serves the new tab (bind-mounted, no rebuild). End-to-end via the :3001 proxy (the browser's own path): admin login + list capabilities (13), create BikeRepair_Yard -> success + file=/app/input/bldg1_capabilities.ttl, named graphs (17), SPARQL amenity COUNT -> 14, delete -> 13 (counts 13->14->13 OK). :3002 service + container + nginx conf removed; docker compose config still valid.

Title: GUI capability delete could report success without persisting
Description: Deleting an amenity not in the GUI-managed capabilities file fell back to a graph-only delete_subject and never edited the owning input/ TTL, so it returned success but reappeared on the next restart; delete_subject also used a no-GRAPH DELETE WHERE that can miss named-graph triples on a stock GraphDB.
Root_Cause: remove_amenity's fallback edited GraphDB only, not the source file; delete_subject's default-graph update is config-dependent.
Fix_Approach: remove_amenity now removes the subject from whichever input/*.ttl defines it (capabilities file or any other building TTL) so the deletion persists; only a subject in NO input file falls back to a (now durable) graph delete. delete_subject made GRAPH-scoped (clears default + all named graphs).
Verification: GRAPH-scoped delete verified on a throwaway GraphDB graph (1 to 0); owning-file edit unit-tested; live create->delete round-trip 13->14->13 post-restart; 479 unit pass.

Title: Non-atomic input/ TTL writes could blank the capabilities graph on a crash
Description: input_ttl_store wrote files with truncate-in-place write_text; a crash mid-write leaves a truncated/empty TTL that ttl_uploader then PUT-replaces into an empty named graph (all amenities gone).
Root_Cause: write_text truncates before writing; no atomic rename.
Fix_Approach: All writes go through _atomic_write (temp file in same dir + fsync + os.replace); original left intact on failure.
Verification: Unit test: failed replace leaves original intact + no temp leak; live create/delete left no stray .tmp; 479 unit pass.

Title: input/ read-modify-write had no cross-process lock (multi-worker data loss)
Description: Concurrent admin writes or multiple workers/replicas sharing the input/ volume could last-writer-wins drop a just-added capability while both returned success. Safe on one uvicorn worker today; latent once scaled (the new rate limiter targets replicas).
Root_Cause: No file lock around the read-modify-write; only safe because the single-worker event loop serialises the synchronous mutation.
Fix_Approach: filelock.FileLock guards each upsert/remove/persist/trash mutation; added filelock to requirements; gitignore the lock + .trash.
Verification: Concurrent-upsert unit test (both survive); 479 unit pass; live round-trip OK.

Title: config-panel esc() did not escape quotes (latent attribute XSS)
Description: esc() escaped only ampersand/lt/gt but values were interpolated into double-quoted HTML data-* attributes (data-drop-graph, data-del-cap); a quote could break out. Low exploitability (values are IRIs/validated ids) but esc() was trusted in an unsafe context.
Root_Cause: esc() lacked quote escaping for attribute context.
Fix_Approach: esc() now also escapes double and single quotes.
Verification: node --check OK; Playwright sweep of all 12 tabs 0 console/page errors.

Title: Admin console had no light theme (dark only)
Description: The single production console (config-panel :3001) was dark-only; the both-light-and-dark requirement was unmet and ~12 hardcoded colors would be dark patches on light.
Root_Cause: Colors partly hardcoded; no prefers-color-scheme / data-theme.
Fix_Approach: Tokenized all surface/detail colors into CSS vars; light palette via @media(prefers-color-scheme:light) + root[data-theme=light]; header toggle persisted to localStorage (default follows OS).
Verification: Playwright light+dark screenshots of overview/ai/ontology render cleanly (no dark patches); toggle auto->light persisted, 0 page errors; dark unchanged.

Title: AI & Models + Overview showed stale Local MiniLM 384-d after the bge-large upgrade
Description: The console hardcoded MiniLM/384-d for the local embedder and a 384<->1536 dim warning, but the live model is bge-large-en-v1.5 @ 1024-d (INFRA-016). Save was safe (only wrote the provider) but the display misinformed operators.
Root_Cause: Hardcoded labels never updated after INFRA-016; ai-config endpoint did not return the model/dim.
Fix_Approach: ai-config now returns embedding_model_local/dimension_local + openai equivalents; console reads them (graceful Local fallback if absent).
Verification: Post-restart ai-config returns bge-large-en-v1.5 / 1024 / 1536; light+dark screenshots show corrected tile.

Title: Redis rate-limit window was not atomic (a crash could 429 an IP forever)
Description: _allow_redis did INCR then a separate EXPIRE; a crash between them leaves a key with no TTL, permanently rate-limiting that IP.
Root_Cause: Two-call INCR/EXPIRE with a gap; only the first increment set the TTL.
Fix_Approach: Replaced with a single atomic Lua eval (INCR + EXPIRE-if-new, plus a TTL<0 re-arm for any leaked keys).
Verification: 5 rapid live requests all 200 post-restart; 479 unit pass.

Title: Orphaned React admin tab duplicates the config-panel Ontology tab
Description: frontend CapabilitiesTab.js + AdminPortal.js reimplement the config-panel Ontology tab but the React app is not served (its compose block is commented out). Untested duplicate that will drift.
Root_Cause: Two admin frontends grew separately; the React one was superseded by the config-panel port (INFRA-020) but left in place.
Fix_Approach: Prepended a NOT-PRODUCTION banner to frontend/README.md flagging the duplication and pointing to config-panel as source of truth. Kept the code (user reviews before any delete).
Verification: Banner added; docker-compose frontend service confirmed commented out.

Title: discover_ttls flat-layout building_id semantics were undocumented
Description: discover_ttls loads every flat input/*.ttl regardless of building_id (FIX-019). Correct for the single active building but a stray second-building TTL in the flat root would cross-load into the single repo.
Root_Cause: The name-agnostic flat load (FIX-019) had no note on the single-building invariant.
Fix_Approach: Added a comment documenting the single-building invariant (contract #1): the active building owns all flat TTLs; a second building must use nested input/<id>/; do NOT add a filename filter (regresses FIX-019).
Verification: Comment added; ttl_uploader unit tests still pass (479 unit).

Title: Datasource-toggle gate intercepted informational/report questions (resolves CAVEAT-017)
Description: _check_locked_capability ran first in routing and fired on any query containing a disabled-source keyword, so 'how do I make a complaint' and 'the toilet is leaking' got 'enable the X System' instead of a real answer.
Root_Cause: The gate keyed on datasource keywords and did not distinguish 'I want live X data' from a policy/how-to/report question.
Fix_Approach: WS-1: the gate now only fires for genuine live-data intents (sensor_data/analytics/trend/anomaly/compare/visualization/compliance); informational/report/capability intents pass through to graph/documents/report_intake.
Verification: Live: 'how do I make a complaint' -> complaint triple (was 'enable Student Complaint System'); 'toilet is leaking' -> maintenance ticket REP-990C49 (was 'enable Water Metering'). New unit test test_gate_silent_for_non_data_intent; 482 unit pass.

Title: TTL-native knowledge topics (procedures / info / maintenance) answered from triples + GUI authoring
Description: Informational/procedural/maintenance questions (complaints, lost property, wifi, reception hours, leaks, broken lift, etc.) had no SPARQL path and were answered by documents or blocked by the toggle gate.
Root_Cause: No vocabulary/instances for non-physical 'capabilities'; only ontosage:Amenity existed.
Fix_Approach: WS-2/3/5: extended the vocab with ontosage:KnowledgeTopic + InformationTopic/Procedure/MaintenanceIssue + answerText/infoUrl/contactEmail/contactPhone/reportTo/steps; 17 curated instances in input/bldg1_knowledge.ttl sourced from cap_*.md (real Estates/IT/Security contacts, nothing fabricated); CapabilityGraphResolver resolves them via UNION and renders answer+contacts+steps; GUI Add-capability form gained the knowledge classes + 6 fields (writes go through input_ttl_store).
Verification: Live: complaint/lost-property/water-leak answered from triples with Estates contacts; GUI create->answerable->delete round-trip of a Procedure topic; 17 KnowledgeTopic in graph; 2 new resolver unit tests; 482 unit pass.
Refs: ontology/ontosage_capabilities.ttl; input/bldg1_knowledge.ttl; orchestrator/services/capability_graph_resolver.py; orchestrator/services/capability_admin.py; orchestrator/main.py; config-panel/html/index.html; config-panel/html/app.js; tests/test_capability_graph_resolver.py

Title: Building-wide floor/room counts now answered from SPARQL
Description: 'how many floors' was not recognized as an inventory-count question and could fall to floor_plan.
Root_Cause: building_metrics inventory regex + snapshot lacked floors/rooms.
Fix_Approach: WS-6: added floor_count/room_count SPARQL COUNT (brick:Floor/brick:Room, namespace-filtered) to BuildingMetrics and 'floors/rooms' to the inventory regex; render includes them. Floor-scoped 'rooms on floor N' still uses the spatial path.
Verification: Live: 'how many floors' -> 'Floors: 8' (graph: 8 floors / 233 rooms confirmed); 482 unit pass.

Title: /health ontology_valid stuck false after a cold start
Description: ontology_validator ran once at startup; if GraphDB wasn't accepting connections yet it cached ok=false and never rechecked, so /health showed ontology_valid=false despite data being loaded.
Root_Cause: One-shot startup validation with no re-check.
Fix_Approach: WS-7: added revalidate_if_needed (cooldown-bounded) called from /health, so the flag self-heals once GraphDB is ready.
Verification: Live: ontology_valid flipped false->true after restart+first /health; 6,850 namespace entities present.

Title: Local LLM down caused silent cascade failures with no guidance
Description: On a cold start the first request to a not-yet-loaded/absent Ollama timed out and tripped the circuit breaker, failing all LLM-dependent answers with no actionable log.
Root_Cause: No startup preflight/warmup for the local model server.
Fix_Approach: WS-8: orchestrator lifespan now pings OLLAMA_BASE_URL, warns with the exact fix ('ollama serve' / 'ollama pull <model>') if unreachable or the model is missing, and warms the model in the background (non-blocking) so the first real request doesn't trip the breaker.
Verification: Reproduced the down-state (battery all-LLM-fail), then verified recovery after starting Ollama; 482 unit pass.

Title: Fuzzy response-cache can cross-contaminate rapid distinct queries
Description: In the AFTER battery, 'show me floor 3' returned the previous question's ('how do I make a complaint') answer. In isolation both answer correctly, so a rapid back-to-back sequence let the fuzzy response-cache return a dissimilar neighbour's answer.
Root_Cause: The response_cache fuzzy-match path appears to match too loosely under rapid distinct queries. Pre-existing (not introduced by this work).
Fix_Approach: CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE: not fuzzy scoring. normalise_query dropped single-char tokens (len>1), so single-digit ids ('floor 3' vs 'floor 5') collapsed to the SAME normalised key -> identical EXACT-cache hash -> one floor's answer served for another. Fix: keep single-DIGIT tokens in normalise_query; plus a defensive fuzzy id-guard (salient_ids) so a >0.85-similar question with a different room/zone id can't fuzzy-hit. 4 unit tests.
Verification: Live: 'noise on floor 3' and 'floor 5' now return DIFFERENT answers (floor 5=33.40 dB, floor 3=no data) instead of a shared cached one; normalise_query('floor 3')!=('floor 5'); 486 unit pass.

Title: OntoSage Conversational Building Vocabulary (OCBV) — publication-ready schema extending Brick
Description: The stakeholder-facing vocabulary (amenities + knowledge topics + properties) was split across a small ontology/ file and only partially documented; there was no single, citable, Brick-extending schema for reuse/publication or as the authoring source of truth.
Root_Cause: The vocab grew incrementally (ROADMAP-009, WS-2) without a consolidated, documented schema.
Fix_Approach: Authored input/ontosage_schema.ttl: one fully-documented (rdfs:label + rdfs:comment + skos:definition + skos:example on every term, worked examples per kind), Brick-EXTENDING (ontosage:locatedIn->brick:Location, aboutEquipment->brick:Equipment, servesFloor->brick:Floor; declares only ontosage: terms, never redefines brick:), building-agnostic TBox: Capability -> Amenity(+10) / KnowledgeTopic(+3) + object/datatype properties + SKOS category scheme. Reduced ontology/ontosage_capabilities.ttl to a stub (single source). The GUI Kind/Type dropdowns mirror these classes. ttl_validator now exempts schema-token files from the per-building @prefix bldg: check (a building-agnostic TBox has none) — which also fixed a startup crash-loop the new schema first triggered.
Verification: Schema parses (218 triples, ~15 classes, 4 obj + 13 data props); loaded live (16 ontosage:Capability subclasses in graph); knowledge topics still answer; 486 unit pass; flake8/black clean.

Title: Guided "Connect a data source" wizard (one-flow onboarding) + Overview CTA
Description: The no-code onboarding path (connect DB -> describe sensors as triples -> verify answerability) existed as three separate, scattered tab actions with no discoverable entry point or enforced sequence; a first-time admin had to know the order and jump between modals.
Root_Cause: Onboarding primitives were built incrementally (add-connection modal, register-sensors modal, per-datasource Verify) without a single guided flow tying them together; discoverability gap flagged as roadmap #4.
Fix_Approach: Added a self-contained 3-step wizard (#wiz-modal): Step 1 pick an existing connection or add a new one (reuses POST /databases; notes the recreate-needed caveat for brand-new creds); Step 2 describe sensors via datalist-guided point rows (reuses the shared dl-classes/dl-locations/dl-uuids suggestions + real UUIDs from /uuids) or CSV paste -> POST /{key}/sensors[/csv]; Step 3 auto-verify via /{key}/answerability with ok/warn/bad verdict and a Restart-service shortcut when a new connection returns no data. Kept in ONE modal so cancelling a step never tears down the flow (avoids the closeModals-closes-all-backdrops pitfall). Launchers: primary "Connect data ->" CTA on Overview + "Guided setup" button on the Databases tab. Parameterized addSensorPointRow(container) for reuse.
Verification: node --check app.js OK; all 32 wizard element IDs present exactly once; live login+chained endpoints return the exact fields the wizard reads (vocab 57 classes/302 locations; energy_data 8 real UUIDs; answerability declared/with_data/level/verdict ok); container serves updated app.js/index.html/style.css; zero Python touched so 486-test suite unaffected. NOTE: no in-browser Playwright walk this session (Playwright MCP unavailable) — verification is static+endpoint-level.

Title: GUI-added datasource never built as an adapter (storage filter dropped custom keys) + Tier-1 hot-apply
Description: A connection added via the admin console/wizard was written to the registry + .env but was NEVER queryable — not even after a restart. Adding it also required a full container recreate to load creds.
Root_Cause: TWO defects: (1) os.environ was not updated when add_database wrote .env, so resolve_connection couldn't expand the new ${VAR} in-process (needed a recreate). (2) AdapterRegistry._initialize_from_yaml applied the building.yaml storage.databases filter to ALL keys, so a custom-overlay (GUI-added) key was merged into the config then SKIPPED at build time — it never became an adapter on reload OR restart. Live-proven: 'merged 1 custom DB([wiztest])' immediately followed by 'skipping 46 unused backends per building.yaml filter', pool stayed at 8.
Fix_Approach: Tier-1 hot-apply (chosen over env-watching or the accept-restart options): (a) add_database now injects the new creds into os.environ right after writing .env; (b) added AdapterRegistry.reload() (lock-serialised close_all -> clear -> initialize) called from the create AND delete endpoints so a connection becomes/stops-being routable with no restart; (c) FIX for the filter bug — _merge_custom_databases records self._custom_keys and _initialize_from_yaml unions them into active_keys, so GUI-added keys (an explicit admin opt-in) are never filtered out. create/delete responses carry hot_applied; wizard + Add-connection notices key off it.
Verification: Live full cycle with a reachable twin connection (mysql_narrow -> energy_data creds): POST /databases -> pool 8->9 with wiztest present and hot_applied=true, NO restart; DELETE -> pool 9->8, wiztest gone, NO restart; overlay file clean. 486 unit pass (no regression) + 3 new registry regression tests; black/flake8 clean.

Title: GraphDB holds duplicate/null-context copies of sensor triples from a historical bulk load
Description: While re-pointing storedAt for FIX-004, found each sensor's triples exist BOTH in the ttl_uploader's per-file named graph (urn:ontosage:ttl:<file>) AND in the ontology-namespace graph (http://.../abacws#, 155k triples) + the null/default context — a second, stale copy from an earlier ingestion mechanism not managed by ttl_uploader.
Root_Cause: A prior bulk/onboard load imported the TTLs into the namespace/default context; ttl_uploader later switched to urn: per-file graphs (PUT-replace) but never cleared the old copies. Re-uploading a file replaces only its urn: graph, leaving the namespace/null-context duplicate — so a storedAt re-point produced CONFLICTING values (old database1 + new database1_floors04) until the stale copy was deleted.
Fix_Approach: MITIGATED for FIX-004: surgically deleted the 628 stale storedAt=database1 triples from the null/default context via a VALUES-restricted batched SPARQL DELETE (safe: only touched the re-pointed uuids). NOT root-fixed: the namespace/null-context duplicate of the WHOLE ontology still exists and will re-conflict on any future re-point. Proper fix = make onboarding/ttl load into a single graph scheme (drop the namespace/default copy, keep only urn: per-file graphs) OR have ttl_uploader clear the namespace graph on load.
Verification: Live: after the targeted DELETE, database1 storedAt dropped 1313->685 and each re-pointed uuid resolves to exactly one storedAt; no functional impact on routing after mitigation. Root duplicate remains (deferred).

Title: Services launcher tab in admin console (attached-tool integrations)
Description: Re-created (and improved) the old Home.png service grid — a launcher where an admin opens each attached tool's web UI (GraphDB, Grafana, Adminer, Qdrant, dashboards…) — inside the :3001 console. Dropped the BrickBot chatbot (OpenWebUI is the chat now).
Root_Cause: The old launcher lived in a separate legacy HTML page; the new console had no single place to reach the stack's tools, and DB data had no browser.
Fix_Approach: Added a data-driven catalog (orchestrator/services/service_catalog.py: id/name/desc/category/icon/host-port+path/internal-probe) + GET /api/v1/admin/services returning the catalog with LIVE online/offline/optional status. New 'Services' nav tab renders category-grouped cards with a status dot and an Open button (URL built from the viewer's own hostname so it works via localhost or a remote IP); optional tools (pgAdmin/ThingsBoard/3D visualiser) are flagged 'enable in docker-compose'. Enabled a lightweight Adminer container (localhost:8093) so sensor/user/report data is browsable. Reachability probe uses a DEDICATED ThreadPoolExecutor with blocking sockets — the app's default executor is saturated, which had stalled in-loop httpx/asyncio probes and falsely marked reachable services offline.
Verification: Live: /api/v1/admin/services returns 8 online (graphdb/qdrant/adminer/file-server/orchestrator/rag/open-webui/ollama), 3 offline (grafana/prometheus/mcp — genuinely not running), 3 optional; Adminer reachable (host :8093 -> 200); config-panel serves the nav item + tab + loadServices + css. 489 unit pass; black/flake8 (new file) clean. Chatbot intentionally excluded.
Refs: orchestrator/services/service_catalog.py; orchestrator/main.py; docker-compose.yml (adminer); config-panel/html/index.html; config-panel/html/app.js; config-panel/html/style.css

Title: GUI-registered sensors persist to input/ + similarity-index rebuild on register & restart
Description: Admin 'Register Sensors' (DatabasesTab CSV/points/TTL) wrote Brick triples straight into a GraphDB named graph (urn:ontosage:db:<key>) with no backing file — lost on a GraphDB volume reset, never reloaded on restart, and never reflected in the RAG similarity index. Now sensors are written TTL-first to input/db_<key>_sensors.ttl (merge/append) and their file graph is synced, so they survive restart (ttl_uploader reloads them) and a GraphDB similarity-index rebuild is auto-enqueued on register + on startup so they surface in semantic RAG.
Root_Cause: db_ontology.register_points/register_ttl bypassed the input_ttl_store source-of-truth layer (used by OntologyTab/Capabilities) and PUT directly to GraphDB; separately, nothing ever rebuilt the GraphDB Ontotext similarity index (bldg_index) the sensor RAG retriever queries — it was only ever built by manually running create_graphdb_index.py.
Fix_Approach: A) register_points/register_ttl delegate to input_ttl_store.persist_ttl_file(merge=True) writing input/db_<key>_sensors.ttl + syncing its urn:ontosage:ttl:<file> graph. B) graph_triple_count(s) retargeted at the file graph; clear_graph trashes the file + drops the legacy graph. C) new ontology_manager.rebuild_similarity_index() + ReindexService 'ontology_similarity' target; register endpoints auto-enqueue it (job_id returned for GUI polling) and the orchestrator lifespan enqueues a background rebuild on startup. D) scripts/backfill_db_sensor_ttls.py dumps pre-existing urn:ontosage:db:* graphs to input/. E) DatabasesTab polls the rebuild job and tells the admin when to ask questions. Refinements after live testing: (a) registration uses UPSERT (persist_ttl_file replace_subjects=True) so re-registering a sensor replaces its triples + external-ref node instead of duplicating (blank-node dup class eliminated); (b) similarity rebuild is DEBOUNCED via services/similarity_reindex.py::SimilarityRebuildDebouncer — a burst of registrations collapses into ONE rebuild and re-runs once if triples arrive mid-rebuild; it is the single similarity-rebuild gateway (register + manual TTL upload + startup + admin reindep all route through it); (c) rebuild = DELETE+CREATE, not the in-place SPARQL rebuildIndex trigger, which was found to hang the index in REBUILDING indefinitely on GraphDB 10.7.4 — delete+create rebuilds the Lucene text index cleanly in ~10s; (d) AUTO-CREATE via POST /rest/similarity (the correct GraphDB 10.x path; /rest/similarity/indexes 405s) so the index self-heals on a fresh volume — no manual Workbench step; (e) admin visibility: GET /api/v1/admin/reindex/similarity-status returns {state,ready,graphdb_status} read live from GraphDB (<index> similarity:status), and DatabasesTab shows a persistent 'Semantic search index: rebuilding/up-to-date' banner + Rebuild-now button so the admin knows when to query OntoSage; (f) manual TTL upload also triggers a rebuild; (g) fixed the DatabasesTab CSV example header (local_id -> local) that made the sample fail the parser. NOTE: had to delete+recreate the live bldg_index once — it was wedged in REBUILDING from an interrupted in-place rebuild.
Verification: 503 unit pass (2 skip); black/isort/flake8(F821,F823)/bandit clean. FULL live E2E (docker, bind-mounted): CSV register -> input/db_<key>_sensors.ttl written + file graph synced; re-register kept the file graph at 16 triples not 32, label replaced, exactly 1 TimeseriesReference node (upsert); 2nd sensor -> 2 distinct sensors (additive); restart reloaded the file via ttl_uploader; manual TTL upload persisted; burst of 3 registrations collapsed into pending (debounce, not 3 rebuilds); similarity-status transitioned pending/OUTDATED -> rebuilding/BUILDING -> idle/BUILT ready=true in ~24s; a brand-new sensor 'VegaSingularSensor' SURFACED in the similarity index at score 0.997 (end-to-end semantic retrieval confirmed); delete+create rebuild reaches BUILT in ~10s. All test artifacts removed (graphs dropped, files+sha-cache scrubbed, no git residue).

Title: ReindexService document indexer wired to wrong app.state attribute (documents reindex is a silent no-op)
Description: _get_reindex_service() reads getattr(app.state,'document_indexer') but the lifespan sets app.state.doc_indexer. So the 'documents' reindex target always gets document_indexer=None and returns skipped='indexer not available' — the KB Reindex 'documents' button does nothing.
Root_Cause: Attribute-name mismatch: app.state.doc_indexer set at startup (~main.py:1016) vs app.state.document_indexer read by the reindex singleton factory (~main.py:3937).
Fix_Approach: FIXED: _get_reindex_service now reads app.state.doc_indexer AND refreshes both indexer refs on every call via new ReindexService.set_indexers() — resolving indexers late so one shared service works whether called early in startup or at request time. This makes it the single indexing gateway used by startup, sensor registration, and manual TTL upload alike.
Verification: Live: document_indexer present on app.state at startup (startup log shows document_indexer ran); startup similarity rebuild now routed through the same gateway (log '[reindex] startup similarity-index rebuild enqueued'). 498 unit pass incl. reindex ontology_similarity dispatch test.

Title: Admin GUI to set the per-building ontology namespace + prefix (building.yaml), as an alternative to hand-editing
Description: Onboarding a new building requires setting the ontology namespace (the URI the bldg: prefix binds to) in input/building.yaml before loading triples. Previously this was only doable by hand-editing the file or via the onboard CLI; there was no GUI and no way to SEE the current value in the admin console. Added a 'Building identity' section (namespace, prefix, name) to the config-panel Ontology tab, always visible + editable, plus a 'Semantic search index' status panel; and documented the prerequisite (file + GUI) in the onboarding guide.
Root_Cause: No admin-console surface for the building namespace/prefix; config.py read ontology_namespace from building.yaml but not a prefix, and nothing wrote building.yaml from the console (only .env had an editor).
Fix_Approach: Backend: GET/PUT /api/v1/admin/building/config (main.py) -> admin_config.read_building_config / write_building_config: validates the namespace is an absolute http(s) URI ending '#' or '/' and the prefix is a valid NCName, then writes ontology_namespace/ontology_prefix/building_name into input/building.yaml via a line-based, comment-preserving, atomic (_set_yaml_scalar + os.replace, value quoting via yaml.safe_dump) writer; config.py now also reads ontology_prefix -> BUILDING_PREFIX at boot. Frontend (config-panel :3001, the real console; the React frontend is testing-only): 'Building identity' form + 'Semantic search index' status/Rebuild-now in the Ontology tab (loadBuildingConfig/saveBuildingConfig/loadSimStatus/rebuildSim), restart-required notice on save. Title: rag-service graphdb_retriever hardcodes the bldg1 namespace -> breaks semantic retrieval for a different building
Description: graphdb_retriever.py builds a prefixes dict with a literal 'bldg': 'http://abacwsbuilding.cardiff.ac.uk/abacws#'. It is used at runtime to shorten IRIs for the LLM and to emit PREFIX declarations for generated SPARQL. For bldg2 (different ontology_namespace) it would fail to shorten that building's IRIs and could emit a wrong bldg: prefix. sparql_agent.py also has a hardcoded instruction to strip the abacws URI from readable names (bldg2 URIs would leak) + a few-shot example using it. Violates design contract #3 (no building literals in runtime code).
Root_Cause: Hardcoded namespace literal instead of reading settings.BUILDING_NAMESPACE / BUILDING_PREFIX (which are now config-driven from building.yaml, incl. the new GUI).
Fix_Approach: FIXED: graphdb_retriever.py now builds the building prefix entry as {settings.BUILDING_PREFIX or 'bldg'}: settings.BUILDING_NAMESPACE (config-driven, from building.yaml). sparql_agent.py: the SPARQL-gen few-shot example's PREFIX bldg URI is interpolated as {settings.BUILDING_NAMESPACE} (in the f-string prompt), and the summary-prompt URI-stripping instruction was reworded to 'show only the local name after the last # or /' (no building literal). Prefix label stays 'bldg' (the project standard); only the namespace URI varies per building. NOTE: rag-service code is baked into its image (not bind-mounted) -> needs a rebuild to apply.
Verification: 511 unit pass; compile+flake8(F821,F823) clean. Live (after docker-compose build graphdb-rag-service + restart both): /graphdb/retrieve returns a building instance (…/abacws#CO2_Level_Sensor_5.06) — the bldg prefix resolves from settings.BUILDING_NAMESPACE (unchanged for bldg1, correct for any building) with no crash; orchestrator /chat 'how many CO2 sensors' returns a reply, confirming the SPARQL prompt builds with the interpolated namespace. Behaviour-preserving for bldg1; portability restored for a 2nd building.

Title: Sensor/equipment COUNT questions misroute to spatial_query (return room counts, not sensor counts)
Description: "How many temperature sensors are there?" is classified spatial_query and answered by the DWG floor-plan/spatial agent (returns building room/area figures, e.g. 'Rooms: 233'), instead of a SPARQL COUNT of brick:Temperature_Sensor on the graph. The sensors exist as triples with UUIDs; only the routing is wrong. routed intent shown live = spatial_query.
Root_Cause: LLM classification prompt rule (dialogue_agent.py:1041) says 'If the user asks for counts, areas, sizes, or adjacency data -> spatial_query' with NO qualification of WHAT is counted, so ALL count questions (incl. sensor/equipment counts that belong to a graph COUNT) map to spatial_query. The deterministic _SPATIAL_BYPASS_PHRASES router did NOT fire (its phrases are all geometric: 'area of floor','adjacent to','largest room','square meters'). Spatial route is legitimate for room geometry (areas/adjacency live in DWG manifests, not RDF) but must not swallow sensor counts.
Fix_Approach: FIXED (defense-in-depth, dialogue_agent.py). (A) Sharpened the LLM classification prompt rule: area/size/adjacency OF ROOMS/SPACES/FLOORS -> spatial_query; a COUNT of sensors/devices/equipment/meters/Brick-class -> metadata (graph COUNT), with explicit examples. (B) Added a deterministic override in _parse_llm_response: (count-trigger _COUNT_TRIGGER_KWS) AND (device word _COUNTABLE_DEVICE_KWS) AND NOT (room-geometry word _ROOM_GEOMETRY_KWS) AND LLM intent in {spatial_query,floor_plan} -> force 'metadata' (routes to sparql node). The spatial_query route is intentionally preserved for real DWG geometry (areas/adjacency the RDF graph does not hold).
Verification: New tests/test_sensor_count_routing.py: 6 sensor-count cases fail-before/pass-after, 6 room-geometry regressions stay spatial_query, 12/12 pass. pytest -m unit = 523 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed (was 511; +12), no regressions; black/isort/flake8(F821,F823) clean. Live (orchestrator restarted, bind-mounted, resp_cache flushed): /chat 'How many temperature sensors are there?' now returns 'There are 210 temperature sensors...' via intent=sensor_data/Building Ontology (was a 233-room spatial_query answer). NOTE: background test_semantic_router/test_non_regression 'failures' were non-unit live/integration tests under 3-way concurrency + restart, not caused by this change.
Refs: orchestrator/agents/dialogue_agent.py (prompt rule ~1041; deterministic guard in _parse_llm_response ~1360; constants _COUNT_TRIGGER_KWS/_COUNTABLE_DEVICE_KWS/_ROOM_GEOMETRY_KWS); tests/test_sensor_count_routing.py; correct target 'metadata'->sparql node (_orchestrator.py:3490)

Title: Analytics questions (e.g. 'What is the energy consumption today?') exceed 120s ('Thinking...') in the live pipeline
Description: In the console Ask tab, 'What is the energy consumption today?' stayed on the 'Thinking... (real pipeline)' placeholder past a 120s client wait; a second question then also stalled (backend contention). energy_data is enabled with 132,688 rows/8 sensors so data exists.
Root_Cause: Not yet root-caused. Hypothesis: analytics intent -> LLM writes Python -> sandboxed code-executor; with local Ollama gemma (large model) the LLM step alone can be tens of seconds, and a single in-flight analytics request appears to serialize/slow subsequent requests. Needs per-stage timing (dialogue vs analytics LLM vs code-executor) to confirm which stage dominates.
Fix_Approach: Root cause was environmental, not pipeline logic: the analytics chain (dialogue -> SPARQL-gen -> analytics codegen, each a local-LLM call) only exceeded the 120s client cap because the primary model gemma4:26b (18GB) does not fit the 16GB laptop GPU and ran ~74% GPU / 26% CPU-offloaded (slow). Switched primary LLM to gpt-oss:20b (~13GB, 100% GPU, ~110 tok/s vs 62). OLLAMA_MODEL in .env.
Verification: Corpus replay 60q on gpt-oss:20b: 0/60 120s-timeouts, avg latency 3.0s / median 0.4s (vs gemma4:26b 240q: 10 timeouts, avg 17.7s). Coverage 91.7% (55/60) vs 26b 82.9%. CAVEAT: recurs if a CPU-offloaded model (e.g. 26b on 16GB VRAM) is reselected — the fix is 'run a model that fits GPU'.

Title: Wind answer states a confident judgement over a raw, unscaled value
Description: RE-TESTED 2026-08-06 on bldg1 and materially worse than the P3 rating implied. 'is the wind strong?' answers: 'Yes - the wind is very strong right now. The most recent reading shows a value of approximately 8308 (the unit used in your data).' The figure is raw and unscaled, the reply admits it does not know the unit, and it still renders a confident 'very strong' verdict on it. A number with no unit cannot support a judgement; presenting one is the same failure class as BUG-123, reached through the analytics path rather than the open-domain answerer. Visible on the demo building for an obvious question.
Root_Cause: SPARQL-gen variance picks direction vs speed sensor; feed values may be stored unscaled / units not applied.
Fix_Approach: New service orchestrator/services/plausibility.py. A verdict is only suppressed when the answer BOTH renders a judgement AND rests on a value outside the range the quantity can take in EVERY unit it is normally reported in - a raw number reported as a raw number needs no caveat, and neither does a verdict over a believable value. The check runs in _response_node where every path's answer converges: the analytics path writes its own prose and never reaches the synthesis pass, which is exactly where this was first seen and why a hook there did nothing. When the caveat is attached, synthesis is additionally forbidden from restating the judgement underneath it. Bounds are facts about the physical world keyed on measurand words from Brick class names, so nothing here knows a site or a sensor id. Two precision fixes came out of testing: a four-digit year and a clock time are excluded before judging (flagging '2026' as an impossible wind speed would discredit the caveat wherever it is right), and a leading minus is captured as a SIGN so -273 is judged as minus 273 - the original test had passed by accident, catching 273 against the upper bound.
Verification: bldg1 live: 'is the wind strong?' and 'how windy is it outside?' now open with the warning and no 'very strong' verdict (was: 'Yes - the wind is very strong right now ... approximately 8308 (the unit used in your data)'). Quiet where it should be: 'temperature on floor 3' answers 27.9 C and 'CO2 level on floor 2' answers in ppm, neither carrying a caveat. tests/test_plausibility.py (30 tests) covers the original failure, believable readings, raw-number reporting, per-measurand ranges, verdict detection, year/clock exclusion, negatives, and a no-building-literals scan. NOTE: the underlying data is still junk - that column ranges 0.14-9998.58 with mean 4506, i.e. synthetic noise rather than wind speed. This fix stops the system asserting a verdict over it; correcting the feed itself is separate.

Title: Qdrant embedding-dimension mismatch breaks document + memory KB
Description: On bldg2, uploading a document (GUI or file-drop) persists the file but the reindex job ERRORS and no documents_<bldg> collection is created; user_memory writes also 400. Qdrant: 'Vector dimension error: expected dim: 3072, got 1024'.

Existing 3072 collection auto-recreated at 1024. Document/capability indexers already used self._embedder.dimension (correct).
Verification: Verified: user_memory recreated 3072->1024 (boot log); documents_bldg2 created dim=1024 + wifi doc indexed (status=indexed, 1 chunk); service-level retrieval returns the wifi chunk (score 0.671). Title: GUI capability delete-to-empty leaves an invalid TTL that crash-loops startup
Description: Deleting the LAST amenity via the admin Capabilities tab left input/<bldg>_capabilities.ttl as comments-only (no @prefix bldg:). The startup TTL validator hard-fails any *.ttl lacking @prefix bldg: → orchestrator 'Application startup failed. Exiting.' → whole stack down (login empty, /chat 000). Masqueraded as 'LLM timeouts' for a long stretch.
Root_Cause: input_ttl_store._serialize_graph prepends only a comment header; rdflib serialises an EMPTY capability graph with NO @prefix lines, so an emptied file loses @prefix bldg:.
Fix_Approach: _serialize_graph now injects the @prefix bldg:/ontosage:/rdfs: block when the serialised body omits it (empty case only; non-empty bodies already declare them). Building-agnostic (namespace from the active building).
Verification: Verified: create amenity then delete the last one via GUI -> file retains @prefix bldg: (grep=1, was 0); orchestrator restarts cleanly. Also repaired the already-broken bldg2_capabilities.ttl by hand.

Title: Embedding decisions followed the PROVIDER name, not the model that is loaded
Description: Two defects with one cause. (1) The retrieval floor was 0.50 if EMBEDDING_PROVIDER == 'local' else 0.35. That 0.50 was calibrated for MiniLM at 384 dimensions; the local model actually loaded is BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 at 1024, and grounding_guard's own docstring warns that under bge-large generic building prose scores high against ANY question. A floor tuned for a model that is not running is worse than no floor, because it looks deliberate. (2) Nothing ever compared an EXISTING Qdrant collection's vector width against the current model. The SHA cache lives INSIDE the collection, so after a model switch unchanged documents skipped re-indexing, the collection kept its old width, and every search failed on a dimension mismatch - silently, because a failed search returns [].
Root_Cause: Provider name was used as a proxy for model identity, and collection width was only ever set at creation, never checked afterwards.
Fix_Approach: (1) MODEL_SCORE_FLOORS moved to module level in shared/config.py, keyed on the model name, with settings.document_score_floor resolving it and DOCUMENT_SCORE_FLOOR available as an explicit override. An unrecognised model falls back to a permissive 0.30 so it under-filters rather than over-filters: showing a weak chunk is recoverable, silently hiding the right one is not. capability_agent now reads that property instead of branching on provider. (2) DocumentIndexer._ensure_dimension compares the stored vector width to the embedder's and drops the collection on a mismatch, forcing a rebuild. It runs BEFORE the SHA cache is read - reading the cache first would report every file unchanged and the stale collection would never be rebuilt - and it fails open, so Qdrant being briefly unavailable cannot stop indexing. STANDARDISATION (2026-08-06, second pass): the deeper fragility was that EMBEDDING_MODEL_* and EMBEDDING_DIMENSION_* are INDEPENDENT settings, and the embedding service read the dimension setting directly. Changing the model and forgetting the dimension therefore built every collection at a width the model never emits - and because vectors of different widths cannot be compared, the failure surfaces later as empty search results rather than an error. A model's width is a fact ABOUT THE MODEL, so the model now settles it: MODEL_DIMENSIONS + dimension_for_model() in shared/config.py, settings.embedding_dimension preferring the model's known width over the configured value and logging any disagreement, and EmbeddingService asking the LOADED model via get_sentence_embedding_dimension() once it is resident - the model itself being the only authority that cannot fall behind. The configured value survives solely as the fallback for a model this build has not seen. BOOT SWEEP (2026-08-06, third pass): each indexer only checked the collection IT owns, and only when that indexer happened to run - a parked building, unchanged documents or already-ingested floor plans were never looked at, so a mismatch could sit unnoticed until a user got an empty answer. Added services/embedding_consistency.py, run in the lifespan BEFORE any indexing, which states the position for the whole instance. It ENUMERATES whatever collections exist rather than checking a list of expected names - that is what makes a building onboarded tomorrow covered the moment it creates one. Derived caches (documents_, capability_, floor_plans, brick_schema) are dropped so their owner rebuilds them; anything holding data that cannot be regenerated (user_memory) is REPORTED and left alone, because an unusable collection is bad but deleting the only copy of something is worse and that call belongs to its owner. Fails open so Qdrant being unavailable cannot block startup.
Verification: Live on bldg1 at the new model-derived floor (0.45 for bge-large): all four document-backed questions still retrieve and cite their declared file (fire_safety.md, room_bookings.md, governance.md, maintenance_log.md). No regressions: the wind caveat, the absent-referent decline and live floor-3 temperature all still behave. tests/test_embedding_standardisation.py (11 tests) covers the per-model floor, the unknown-model fallback, the override, agreement between the running model and its floor, drop-on-mismatch, leave-alone-on-match, absent collection, fail-open, and a source assertion that the width check precedes the SHA read. STANDARDISATION verified: an audit of every live collection found three still at 384 (MiniLM-era) while the running model emits 1024 - documents_bldg2, capability_bldg2 and brick_schema (86,157 points). None was causing a live failure: documents_bldg2 belongs to a parked building and would have been rebuilt automatically on activation, while capability_bldg2 and brick_schema serve dead paths (the capability KB, TODO-081, and SemanticOntologyAgent, which is exported but never instantiated). All three were dropped; the four that remain - capability_bldg1, documents_bldg1, floor_plans, user_memory - are all 1024 and agree with the model. Answers unaffected: document retrieval, service history, live floor-3 temperature and the absent-referent decline all still behave. tests/test_embedding_standardisation.py now 21 tests, including the exact drift case (model switched to MiniLM, dimension left at 1024 - the model wins) and a check that the running configuration is internally consistent. BOOT SWEEP verified live, including the repair path rather than just the happy case. Clean boot logs '[embedding] 4 collections all at 1024d, matching BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5' and runs before the document indexer. Repair proven end to end by planting a 384d collection under a building name that has never existed (documents_neversite) and restarting: the sweep found it, dropped it and logged why, with no code aware of that building. Answers unaffected afterwards - 6/6 on document retrieval, service history, live temperature, absent-referent decline, the plausibility caveat and the equipment census. tests/test_embedding_consistency.py (14 tests) covers the consistent case, drop-derived, report-irreplaceable, an unseen building, an empty instance, an unreadable collection mid-sweep, Qdrant down, and a no-building-literals scan.

Title: Generic sensor count + building-info misroute to sensor_data then capability fallback
Description: 'how many sensors does this building have?' and 'what building is this / how many floors?' answer 'I don't have a capability profile on record' instead of 326 sensors / BuildSys 3 floors. Specific-type count works ('how many temperature sensors' -> 136).
Root_Cause: Dialogue routes generic/whole-building metadata questions to sensor_data (no specific UUID resolves) which then falls through to the capability agent; the empty capability KB returns the 'no profile' message. Should route to metadata -> SPARQL COUNT.
Fix_Approach: Two building-agnostic fixes. (1) dialogue_agent: the LLM correctly classified metadata but a later data-query override flipped metadata->sensor_data (is_data_query matched the 'sensor' noun); added a guard so a countable/structure/building-identity question (TBOX-count phrasing: _COUNT_TRIGGER_KWS + _COUNTABLE_DEVICE/_STRUCTURE_COUNT_KWS, or _BUILDING_INFO_KWS) is never demoted. (2) capability_agent: the workflow inventory-count override routes counts to the capability node, which early-returned 'no profile' when kb is None (bldg2 has no capability.yaml) BEFORE the KB-independent live-metrics grounding; moved the TBOX-COUNT live-metrics grounding ABOVE the kb-None guard, display name resolved from building.yaml. (3) sparql_agent: added TBOX templates (generic COUNT brick:Sensor via rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf*, brick:Building rdfs:label) as the metadata-path backup.
Verification: Live bldg2: 'how many sensors' -> 326 (533 points/3 floors/52 rooms); 'how many floors' -> 3; 'what building is this' -> bldg2 (BuildSys ontology). Typed-count regression intact ('temperature sensors' -> 136). All keyed on brick:Sensor/Floor/Building TBOX, no building literals.

Title: Live 'last N hours' analytics finds no readings despite fresh data
Description: 'average air temperature over the last 6 hours' -> 'No readings were found' even though the publisher wrote rows up to now (wide sensor_data, latest 16:27 UTC). Earlier a one-off worked (21.49C).
Root_Cause: Likely a timezone/window mismatch (data timestamps UTC vs the analytics 'now' window) or the analytics agent resolving to a UUID/column with no recent rows. Needs tracing of the SQL window the analytics agent builds vs the wide-table datetime.
Fix_Approach: Two root causes, both fixed building-agnostic. (1) PRIMARY: MySQLAdapter.validate_query used sql.split()[0], yielding the token '(SELECT' for the parenthesized '(SELECT...) UNION ALL (SELECT...)' multi-UUID wide-table query -> failed the SELECT allow-list -> 'Only SELECT queries are allowed' -> sql_rows=0 for EVERY window (even 30-day). Fixed: lstrip leading '(' + whitespace before identifying the first keyword. (Postgres/SQLite/sql_agent guards already accept '(' via startswith; only the mysql adapter was broken.) (2) SECONDARY: server tz is BST(+1) but data is naive UTC, so DATE_SUB(NOW(),INTERVAL 1 HOUR) started AFTER the newest UTC row -> empty sub-offset windows. Fixed: pin the adapter session to UTC (create_pool init_command SET time_zone='+00:00') to match OntoSage's UTC storage convention.
Verification: Live bldg2: 'avg temp last 24h' -> 18.84C; 'last 2h' -> 21.29C (real averaged data w/ per-type breakdown). DB-level 1h window now returns 14 rows (was 0 pre-fix). Building-agnostic: UTC storage convention + wide-table UNION shape, no building literals.

Title: Document-KB (policy/manual) not surfaced by the capability agent

Doc score floor already relaxed to 0.28 for local embeddings.
Verification: Live bldg2: 'what is the wifi policy?' and 'how do I connect to the guest wifi?' -> surfaces the Bldg2 Wifi doc (BuildSys-Guest open + captive portal; BuildSys-Secure staff). Building-agnostic: any building with documents_<bldg> is now surfaced with no capability.yaml required.

Title: Cross-floor compare deflects (bldg2 sensors have no floor linkage)
Description: 'compare temperature between floor 0 and floor 1' returned 'requires sensors with linked time-series data' — the floor-scoped SPARQL resolved 0 sensors per floor.
Root_Cause: TWO causes: (1) bldg2 sensors had NO spatial topology in the ontology (no brick:hasLocation; rooms not linked to floors on the sensor-referenced zone entities), so the floor-scoped resolver's sensor->hasLocation->space->isPartOf->floor chain matched nothing; (2) the empty SPARQL result was CACHED (sparql_cache:* / cache:sparql_exec:*) from the pre-fix run and replayed, masking the fix.
Fix_Approach: (1) New building-agnostic scripts/generate_spatial_topology.py: reads floors + spaces + timeseries sensors from the active graph, links each room-encoded sensor to its space (a dot-segment of the sensor name that matches a known space) and distributes referenced spaces evenly across floors (brick:hasLocation + brick:isPartOf). Writes input/<id>_spatial_topology.ttl (auto-loaded by ttl_uploader next boot) + uploads to GraphDB. (2) Flush the SPARQL result cache after topology/data changes.
Verification: Live bldg2: sensor->floor now resolves 17/17/16; 'compare temp floor 0 vs 1' -> Floor0 22.27C vs Floor1 22.25C; 'floor 1 vs 2' -> 22.27 vs 22.29 (distinct per-floor, close because synthetic zone data is uniform). ttl_uploader auto-loaded bldg2_spatial_topology.ttl on restart (named graph). NOTE gotcha: flush sparql_cache:* + cache:sparql_exec:* after graph edits or the old empty result is replayed.

Title: bldg3 ontology had 3 malformed-reference defects breaking SQL/analytics + boot (fixed on onboarding)

Title: Boot-order race: validator + sensor-map regen run before ttl_uploader finishes
Description: On a cold boot with a not-yet-loaded graph, the lifespan runs OntologyValidator and the sensor-map auto-regen BEFORE startup TTL ingestion completes: validator logs a false "No entities found" error (self-heals on its later re-run), and the sensor-map regen is skipped entirely because the graph looks empty — leaving no input/.sensor_map.cache.json until a manual orchestrator restart. Observed live on bldg1 swap-back 2026-07-29 (validator errored 17:03:49, ttl_uploader done 17:04:33, map only appeared after restart at 17:17).
Root_Cause: main.py lifespan ordering: validator/sensor-map steps are not sequenced after (or retried until) ttl_uploader completion.
Fix_Approach: Three-part fix: (1) Phase 1 (validate->introspect->sensor-map->detector) wrapped as re-runnable _ontology_phase1() in main.py lifespan; (2) after startup TTL ingestion, re-run iff init was skipped OR new TTLs uploaded (uploads force a sensor-map rebuild; nothing-new + already-inited = no-op); plus a background backstop retrying up to ~7min for slow GraphDB warm-up; (3) ontology_validator existence check now a LIMIT-1 probe (30s) with the expensive full COUNT demoted to informational (60s, non-fatal) — the old 20s COUNT over 16.6M cold triples always timed out.
Verification: Live race test: docker compose restart graphdb orchestrator -> Phase 1 failed (GraphDB not reachable), post-ingestion retry passed at 09:58:35 (1965 entities, all checks passed), startup completed, /health 200 — zero manual restarts. 523 unit tests pass.

Verification: grep: 0 wide-table INSERTs in publisher; registry shows floors04/synth nature:synthetic; TTL routing 680->database1 / 522->database1_floors04 / 106->database1_synth.

Title: automation_capability node crashed on string entities — ALL automation questions returned empty
